era: The Scandal: NEET-UG Leak & CBSE Marking Crisis

events.title: NEET-UG 2026 Exam Held for 2.27 Million Candidates
events.detail: The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Undergraduate) is conducted nationwide for over 2.27 million aspirants seeking admission to India's medical and dental colleges. Within days, allegations surface of a leaked question paper circulating before the exam.

events.title: CBSE Class 12 Results Trigger On-Screen Marking (OSM) Controversy
events.detail: CBSE declares Class 12 results using On-Screen Marking (OSM), a digital evaluation system introduced at scale for the first time. Within days, complaints flood in of unexpectedly low marks in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, blurred scans, and multi-page answers evaluated only partially. CBSE later identifies roughly 5,000 blurred-sheet cases and 23 instances of answer sheets belonging to a different candidate, out of about 98 lakh sheets from 18 lakh candidates.

events.title: NTA Cancels NEET-UG 2026, Refers Case to CBI
events.detail: The National Testing Agency, with government approval, cancels the NEET-UG 2026 examination after investigators find substantial overlap between a pre-circulated 'guess paper' and the actual question paper. The matter is referred to the Central Bureau of Investigation.

events.title: CBI Arrests Chemistry Professor Over Paper Access
events.detail: CBI arrests chemistry professor P. V. Kulkarni, who had access to the NEET question papers through his work as a translator for the NTA, as the first arrest in the paper-leak investigation.

events.title: Cockroach Janta Party Founded as Satirical Response
events.detail: Digital communications strategist Abhijeet Dipke founds the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical youth movement, after Chief Justice of India Surya Kant compares unemployed youth and social-media activists to 'cockroaches' and 'parasites'. The name is adopted as a badge of protest identity.

events.title: Coaching Institute Owner Arrested in Leak Probe
events.detail: CBI arrests coaching institute owner Shivraj Motegaonkar as investigators trace the network allegedly responsible for circulating the leaked NEET question paper.

events.title: School Headmistress Arrested Over Physics Paper Leak
events.detail: CBI arrests school headmistress Manisha Sanjay Havaldar in connection with the leak of the NEET physics paper, widening the scope of the investigation beyond the initial suspects.

events.title: Supreme Court Seeks Status Report on NEET Probe
events.detail: The Supreme Court of India seeks a status report from investigators on the progress of the NEET-UG paper leak probe and prior recommendations for exam-security reform.

events.title: Physics Teacher and Pediatrician Among Further Arrests
events.detail: CBI makes additional arrests, including physics teacher Tejas Harshadkumar Shah and pediatrician Manoj Shirure, as the investigation into the paper-leak network continues to expand.

events.title: Student Groups Protest Outside Ministry of Education
events.detail: The All India Students' Association (AISA) and Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS) hold an early protest outside the Ministry of Education demanding accountability for the NEET leak and CBSE OSM irregularities, ahead of the larger CJP-led mobilization.

events.title: CJP Launches First Jantar Mantar Protest
events.detail: Abhijeet Dipke arrives from the United States and the Cockroach Janta Party launches its first street protest at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi. Delhi Police deploy roughly 5,000 personnel across the district. Hundreds gather, including students, parents, doctors, lawyers and teachers, marking the start of what becomes a 50-day occupation.

events.title: Delhi High Court Upholds Temporary Telegram Ban
events.detail: The Delhi High Court upholds a temporary government ban on the Telegram messaging app, imposed amid concerns the platform was used to circulate the leaked NEET paper and coordinate unauthorized exam-related content.

events.title: Police Cut Lights, Restrict Food and Water at Protest Site
events.detail: As demonstrators regroup at Jantar Mantar for an extended mobilization, Delhi Police employ pressure tactics including cutting lighting and restricting food and water access until a 5 p.m. deadline. Dipke refuses to leave the site until Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.

events.title: Re-NEET Administered With Enhanced Security
events.detail: The rescheduled NEET-UG examination is conducted nationwide under enhanced security measures, including biometric checks and stricter frisking, intended to prevent a repeat of the May leak.

events.title: Sonam Wangchuk Joins Protest, Begins Indefinite Hunger Strike
events.detail: Ladakhi environmentalist and education reformer Sonam Wangchuk joins the CJP-led agitation at Jantar Mantar and begins an indefinite hunger strike alongside six All India Students' Association members, including national president Neha Bora and activist Hamad, demanding Pradhan's resignation.

events.title: CJP Launches Nationwide 'Pradhan Go Back' Campaign
events.detail: The Cockroach Janta Party launches a coordinated nationwide 'Pradhan Go Back' digital and street campaign, escalating pressure for the Education Minister's resignation beyond Delhi.

events.title: Re-NEET Results Declared, 110,000 Qualify
events.detail: The National Testing Agency declares results for the rescheduled NEET-UG exam; approximately 110,000 candidates qualify, more than six weeks after the original exam date, deepening the admissions-cycle backlog for medical colleges.

events.title: Wangchuk's Health Deteriorates on Day 19 of Fast
events.detail: By the 19th day of his hunger strike, Sonam Wangchuk has lost 9.1 kilograms; medical evidence shows muscle loss and mobility impairment, raising alarm among supporters and medical observers.

events.title: Police Forcibly Remove Wangchuk, Admit Him to Hospital
events.detail: Delhi Police forcibly remove Sonam Wangchuk from the protest site and admit him to Safdarjung Hospital. In response, Dipke begins his own indefinite hunger strike, and Students' Federation of India leaders Adarsh M. Saji and Aishe Ghosh announce they will join the fast. Dipke warns that suppression of the protest would spark citywide demonstrations.

events.title: 'Sansad Chalo' March Met With Tear Gas and Pellet Guns
events.detail: Tens of thousands gather at Jantar Mantar and attempt to march toward Parliament during the monsoon session. Security forces deploy lathis, tear gas and pellet guns. Delhi Police report 118 personnel injured; hospital sources report 60+ protesters injured with 65+ medico-legal cases logged at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital by 7 p.m. The CJP claims roughly 150 protesters hospitalized and 70 detained. Delhi Metro closes 5 stations and internet service is suspended near Parliament.
events.confidenceReason: Injury and detention figures diverge sharply between Delhi Police, hospital records, and CJP claims.

events.title: DCP Filmed Slapping Female Protester
events.detail: Video footage circulates showing DCP Sandeep Lamba appearing to slap a female protester during the July 20 crackdown. Activist Saket Gokhale files an FIR complaint over the incident; Gurdwara Bangla Sahib becomes a refuge for injured and displaced demonstrators as police close in on the protest site.
events.confidenceReason: Footage widely circulated but no confirmed departmental inquiry outcome as of Jul 25.

events.title: Wangchuk Transferred to Medanta; Congress Leaders Detained
events.detail: The Delhi High Court orders Wangchuk transferred from Safdarjung to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram at his own request. Separately, Congress MPs led by Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi march to Prime Minister Modi's residence in protest; police detain the opposition leaders before releasing them hours later. Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya's bench declines to hold an urgent hearing on allegations of excessive police force.

events.title: Protests Spread to Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Beyond
events.detail: Solidarity protests erupt in Mumbai, Chandigarh, Surat, Patna, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kerala, Lucknow and Kolkata despite heavy overnight rain in Delhi. The Ministry of Home Affairs deploys 20 CRPF companies from Kolkata; Delhi Metro closes 16 stations. Chief Justice Surya Kant separately rejects a petition on police brutality, declining to review video evidence.

events.title: Delhi HC Agrees to Hear PIL Seeking NIA Probe Into CJP Funding
events.detail: A PIL filed by Satish Kumar Aggarwal, former vice-president of the Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha, alleges the CJP protest movement was backed by foreign-funded organizations as part of a broader conspiracy, and seeks an NIA investigation plus transfer of related FIRs. The Delhi High Court agrees to hear the plea the following day.
events.confidenceReason: Foreign-funding allegation is an unproven claim in a pending PIL, not an established fact.

events.title: Modi Announces Fast-Track Courts; Wangchuk Ends 26-Day Fast
events.detail: PM Modi announces fast-track courts for paper-leak prosecutions; the Delhi High Court establishes one within hours. Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh Rana give Sonam Wangchuk written assurances on withdrawing cases against non-violent protesters, holding leak-prevention discussions, and compensating suicide victims' families. Wangchuk breaks his 26-day hunger strike on this basis, having lost significant weight and mobility.

events.title: MEA Dismisses Foreign-Funding Allegations Against CJP
events.detail: The Ministry of External Affairs dismisses allegations that the Cockroach Janta Party received foreign funding, with a spokesperson saying it has 'no information to share' supporting the claim. Dipke announces the protest will continue until Pradhan resigns, despite Wangchuk's fast ending the day before.

events.title: Pradhan Resigns; CJP Calls Off Protests
events.detail: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns, posting a two-page letter addressed to 'my young friends' taking moral responsibility for the exam failures while defending the government's crisis response. Hours later, amid a fresh round of tear-gas dispersal near Jantar Mantar (in which a Special Commissioner and two officers are injured by stone-pelting), the CJP calls off its protests in a joint press conference with Ministers Nadda and Rana, securing commitments to withdraw police cases against non-violent protesters in NDA-ruled states, take no future punitive action, and pay maximum compensation to suicide victims' families under existing rules.

events.title: International Solidarity Rallies Include Greta Thunberg in London
events.detail: Solidarity demonstrations with the Indian youth movement are held in London (Trafalgar Square, with climate activist Greta Thunberg), Manchester, Edinburgh, Glasgow, New York City, Los Angeles, San Jose and Dublin, reflecting the diaspora and international attention the movement drew during its peak.

events.title: Lok Sabha Passes Public Examinations Amendment Bill
events.detail: The Lok Sabha passes the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by voice vote after extensive discussion. The bill strengthens the 2024 law, increasing the prison term for exam malpractice from 3–5 years to 5–10 years, raising the maximum fine from ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh, and mandating fast-track courts in every state and union territory.

events.title: Rajya Sabha Clears Exam Amendment Bill; Becomes Law
events.detail: The Rajya Sabha passes the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by voice vote, a day after the Lok Sabha, completing the legislative response demanded by protesters and clearing the way for fast-track courts and time-bound investigation of exam-related offences nationwide.

events.title: NTA Orders Re-Conduct of Three UGC-NET Papers
events.detail: Barely three weeks after the exam-amendment law takes effect, the NTA announces it will re-conduct three UGC-NET June 2026 papers — English, Commerce and Sociology — after an internal committee finds multiple errors following student complaints, including 67 of 150 English questions repeated from the 2024 exam. The re-tests are scheduled for Sep 9 (English, Commerce) and Sep 10 (Sociology), with no extra fee charged to candidates; results for the other 84 subjects proceed as scheduled. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi calls for accountability, reviving scrutiny of the NTA's reliability.

media.caption: NTA announces fresh UGC-NET exams for English, Commerce and Sociology after finding widespread errors and repeated questions.

events.title: NSUI Stages Protest Against NTA Over UGC-NET Irregularities
events.detail: The Congress-affiliated National Students' Union of India (NSUI) protests outside the NTA office in Delhi against the UGC-NET June 2026 irregularities, arguing the episode shows the agency has not been meaningfully reformed despite the NEET crisis and the new amendment act. Delhi Police and CRPF personnel detain demonstrators after protesters attempt to breach barricades; NSUI says several of its members were injured during the police action. NSUI national president Vinod Jakhar demands the NTA chairman's resignation, saying 'the mistake is NTA's, but the punishment is for the students' — keeping public trust in national testing infrastructure a live issue as the movement's 75th day passes.

media.caption: NSUI members clash with police outside the NTA office in Delhi during a protest over UGC-NET irregularities.

era: Parallel Front: Jharkhand JPSC/JSSC Recruitment Protests

events.title: Job Aspirants Launch JPSC/JSSC Recruitment Protest in Ranchi
events.detail: Hundreds of students and government-job aspirants begin an open-ended sit-in at Bapu Vatika in Ranchi, Jharkhand, demanding a CBI probe into alleged paper leaks and malpractice in Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) recruitment exams, including those outsourced to private vendor TSR Data Processing Pvt Ltd (TDPL). Organized under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch banner and led by Jharkhand Loktantrik Kranti Morcha figure Devendra Nath Mahto, the protest relocates to Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium on Jul 29 as it grows — a parallel, state-level youth exam-integrity movement distinct from the NEET/CBSE-driven Jantar Mantar protests in Delhi.

media.caption: Job aspirants march in Ranchi during the JPSC/JSSC recruitment-exam protests.

events.title: Devendra Nath Mahto Begins Indefinite Hunger Strike
events.detail: Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto begins an indefinite hunger strike at the Ranchi protest site, later joined by fellow organizers Umme Habiba and Rahul Kranti and several other aspirants, escalating pressure on the Hemant Soren government to cancel tainted JPSC/JSSC exams and order a federal probe.

media.caption: Devendra Nath Mahto, who led an indefinite hunger strike at the Ranchi protest site.

events.title: 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' March Met With Tear Gas and Water Cannons
events.detail: Thousands of job aspirants attempt to march roughly four kilometers to the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly in Ranchi on the protest's 17th day. More than 1,500 security personnel deploy barbed-wire barricades; police fire tear gas and water cannons and use batons after protesters break through several barricades near Jagannathpur Temple. Several protesters and at least four police personnel are injured. Devendra Nath Mahto, then nine days into his hunger strike, joins the march by ambulance. Hours later the state government offers a partial concession — cancelling the 14th JPSC preliminary exam and two backlog tests, with three JPSC board members resigning — but protesters reject this as insufficient absent a CBI probe and cancellation of the JSSC-CGL exam.

media.caption: Riot police deploy water cannons and barricades against job aspirants marching toward the Jharkhand Assembly, Aug 10, 2026.

events.title: CID Raids JSSC Office; 20 Arrested Including Ex-Chairman
events.detail: Jharkhand's Criminal Investigation Department searches the JSSC office in Ranchi on the protest's 24th day, part of a widening probe into recruitment-exam irregularities. CID ADG Manoj Kaushik confirms the raids; investigators have by this point arrested 20 people connected to the recruitment scandal, including former JPSC chairman L. Khiangte. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi urges Chief Minister Hemant Soren to personally meet the protesting students, noting the demonstrations have remained peaceful.

media.caption: Demonstrators during the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march in Ranchi, around the time of the CID's raid on the JSSC office.

events.title: Soren Government Cancels JSSC-CGL and All TDPL Exams; Mahto Ends Fast
events.detail: After a marathon Cabinet meeting, Chief Minister Hemant Soren announces Jharkhand will cancel the JSSC Combined Graduate Level (CGL) exam and every recruitment examination, result and selection conducted by outsourced vendor TDPL since 2014, and forms an exam-reforms committee headed by senior IAS officer Amitabh Kaushal. The state also blacklists TDPL. Devendra Nath Mahto, Umme Habiba and Rahul Kranti end their 16-day hunger strike as state ministers Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari offer them juice; Mahto calls it 'a huge victory for Jharkhand' while reiterating the unmet demand for a CBI probe. The government declines the CBI demand, citing Supreme Court/High Court monitoring of the JSSC-CGL process, and instead proposes an expert panel drawn from ISM Dhanbad, IIM Ranchi and XLRI Jamshedpur.

media.caption: File photo of Devendra Nath Mahto, who ended his 16-day hunger strike after the Jharkhand government cancelled the tainted exams.

events.title: Planned Gherao of CM Soren's Residence Called Off
events.detail: The JPSC-JSSC Abhiyarthi Reform Manch calls off its threatened Aug 20 siege of Chief Minister Hemant Soren's residence and cancels plans to burn his effigy, citing the government's Aug 17 exam-cancellation decision. Mahto warns the fight is not over, saying 'I have ended my hunger strike, not the protest,' and announces a second phase of agitation demanding a monitoring committee, independent audits and guarantees against future paper leaks.

media.caption: Devendra Nath Mahto announces the gherao is called off, but the protest continues into a second phase.

events.title: High Court Stays Cancellation of JPSC and JSSC-CGL Exams
events.detail: The Jharkhand High Court grants interim stays blocking the state government's cancellation orders — first on Aug 20 for the 11th–13th JPSC exams and the Food Safety Officer recruitment, then on Aug 21 for the JSSC-CGL and CDPO exams — after roughly 2,000 candidates who had already secured appointments challenge the cancellations as a due-process violation. Justice Deepak Roshan's order lets successful candidates keep their posts pending investigation, while warning that anyone later found to have benefited from fraud will still lose their job. The court sets the next hearing for Sep 15, 2026 and orders all parties to file affidavits; separately, the Supreme Court is due to hear a plea seeking a CBI probe into the recruitment-exam irregularities.

media.caption: The Jharkhand High Court stayed the state's cancellation of JPSC and JSSC-CGL recruitment exams pending further hearings.

events.title: Students Burn Soren Effigies, Clash With Police After HC Stay
events.detail: The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Forum calls for effigy-burning protests against Chief Minister Hemant Soren across all 24 Jharkhand districts in response to the High Court's stay order, with the largest rally drawing hundreds to Gandhi Maidan in Ranchi and further clashes reported in Hazaribag and Giridih. Protesters accuse the state government of 'betrayal' for failing to adequately defend the exam cancellations in court, and allege police and JMM workers used force including assaulting female demonstrators after some marchers deviated from their approved route. Ranchi City DCP K.V. Raman says police used only 'mild force' after protesters disregarded the route given by the administration.

media.caption: Students protest at Gandhi Maidan, Ranchi, after the Jharkhand High Court stayed exam cancellations, Aug 22, 2026

events.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice on Separate JPSC Exam-Rigging Plea
events.detail: The Supreme Court issues notices to the central government, the Jharkhand government, the JPSC and the CBI on a separate Article 32 petition filed by social activist Harisharan Devgan, alleging a candidate qualified the April 19, 2026 Combined Civil Services Preliminary exam despite attempting only 48 of 100 questions on Paper I, based on a carbon-copy OMR sheet circulated on social media. The petition seeks either a CBI investigation or an inquiry led by a retired Supreme Court judge. Chief Justice Surya Kant — whose May 2026 remark comparing unemployed youth to 'cockroaches' gave the broader protest movement its name — tells the bench: 'These are not inquiries. This is an investigation. There is forensic examination required or something else,' signaling the court's own skepticism of the state's internal probes.

media.caption: Supreme Court of India, which issued notice on a plea alleging JPSC exam rigging, Aug 24, 2026

era: New Front: Bihar BPSC/TRE-4 Exam Protests

events.title: BPSC Exam Controller Suspended Over 'Dogs Bark' Remark
events.detail: Bihar Public Service Commission examination controller Rajesh Kumar Singh, questioned by reporters about the ongoing student agitation over the 70th BPSC prelims and the TRE-4 teacher-recruitment format, invokes the Hindi proverb 'Hathi chale bazaar, kutta bhaunke hazar' ('the elephant walks through the market while a thousand dogs bark'), widely read as dismissing protesting students as barking dogs. The remark goes viral and draws sharp backlash, including from Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav, who demands a public apology. Singh says the quote was 'twisted and presented out of context' with no intent to hurt anyone's sentiments, but Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary orders his suspension the same day.

events.title: Patna Students Clash With Police Over 70th BPSC Exam and TRE-4 Format
events.detail: Thousands of BPSC and teacher-recruitment aspirants, joined by AISF, DYFI and NSUI activists, march roughly 5 km from Gandhi Maidan toward Raj Bhavan and Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's residence, demanding cancellation of the 70th BPSC preliminary exam over alleged paper leaks, a single-stage TRE-4 format, an end to negative marking, and full domicile-based recruitment. Police block the march at JP Golambar and the Dak Bungalow roundabout; when protesters break through barricades, officers respond with a lathi-charge and water cannons. A female demonstrator is found unconscious in the crush and several students are detained. Union minister Chirag Paswan visits the site to meet aspirants after the clash.

media.caption: Students clash with police after breaking barricades on the march toward Raj Bhavan, Patna, Aug 25, 2026

events.title: CM Choudhary Concedes: TRE-4 to Be Held in a Single Phase
events.detail: Two days after the Patna clashes, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary meets a student delegation and announces the fourth Teacher Recruitment Examination (TRE-4) will be conducted in a single stage rather than the planned two-phase preliminary-and-mains format. The government unveils nine other measures, including a Patna High Court judge-led Expert Committee on Examination Reforms to review the 70th BPSC exam and hear grievances, a promised Bihar Staff Selection Commission examination calendar, and an inquiry into the 1,799-post sub-inspector recruitment exam. Two students who had been on hunger strike at Gardanibagh since Aug 18 end their fast by taking juice, though the core demand to cancel the 70th BPSC exam remains unmet.

media.caption: Bihar government announces TRE-4 exam reforms after student protests, Aug 27, 2026
